pending_commit.commit_message: bobba: add blorb and droid into the support of controlling USB Type-A power. Blorb and droid are first projects we are tyring to enable the control of USB Type-A power in the run time. This CL set inhibit_charging_in_suspend to USB_DISALLOW_SUSPEND_CHARGE in default and relies on OS to change this flag based on the status of USB device on the USB Type-A port. BUG=b:130767435 BRANCH=octopus TEST=1. `make BOARD=bobba -j4` 2. check power of USB Type-A port is disabled when OS gets into S0iX and no any USB device is ever connected to DUT. CHROMIUM: ARM: dts: rockchip: Throttle DDR frequency on mickey to 433 MHz when CPU gets warm DDR frequency changes are expensive, use a discrete step instead of a range to avoid continuous back and forth switching by the thermal framework. Switching the DDR frequency is very time sensitive, the code bumps temporarily the CPU frequency to increase the chances to perform the change in time. Note that the trip point for capping the DDR frequency is slightly below the first trip point for throttling the CPU. This may avoid CPU frequency bumps just for changing the DDR frequency. BUG=chromium:941638 TEST=on mickey: DDR frequency is capped to 433 MHz for T_cpu >= 63C Change-Id: Ic952fe552603b58e1057d23913d10398f848a751 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1622709 Commit-Ready: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>

tael(-arc): Do not set USE=device_tree USE=device_tree tells the kernel ebuild to build all device trees for the platform and bundle them together with the kernel binary into a FIT image. Crostini (tael) kernels do not use FIT images but instead load the kernel binary directly together with an auto-generated device tree. Therefore, they shouldn't need this. BUG=None TEST=None Change-Id: Icec0a5634708ab5f7f35e164aa57d08cc6644c3d Signed-off-by: Julius Werner <jwerner@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1626214 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Sonny Rao <sonnyrao@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: arm64: dts: mt8183-kukui: Drive cr50 SPI CS pin as GPIO After entering sleep, cr50 requires a short pulse on the chip select line to get out of sleep. cr50_spi driver does this by sending a single transfer, without any data, with a 1ms delay. The MTK SPI controller does not assert CS in that case, defeating the purpose of the call, as the HW does not send the wake pulse. Switch to controlling the CS pin using normal GPIO, which the kernel asserts in common code, and makes it possible to pulse it. BUG=b:133458651 TEST=Hack cr50_spi to always try to wake cr50, see that there is a 1ms pulse before all transactions. TEST=With servo_micro connected, one should never see cr50_spi spi0.0: Timeout during flow control in the logs. Change-Id: I57c76913c51ac3da94bf0740a8df52012ebd94dd Signed-off-by: Nicolas Boichat <drinkcat@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1628409 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Pi-Hsun Shih <pihsun@chromium.org>
